methodology.section_counts: Direct grep (Select-String) per pack file for '"Section": "([A-F])"' — verified 2026-07-27
methodology.difficulty_by_pack: Provided by S831 coordinator from known pack-level data
methodology.per_section_difficulty: Estimated by proportional split (template-generated rotation groups distribute difficulty evenly across sections within each pack)
methodology.limitations: Per-item Section+Difficulty cross-tab would require boundary-aware object parsing (DL-020 risk). Proportional estimate is reliable given rotation-group templating.

pack_d.note: Section regex matched 499; 1 item has Section field that did not match standard pattern (line-split artifact). QuestionID count confirms 500.

pool_difficulty_actual_vs_target.summary: Pool is severely compressed toward the lower half of the difficulty scale. Moderate (48.3%) is the dominant label — 18pp above target. Difficult+VD combined = 3.3% vs 35% target. The 'missing' 31.7pp is distributed across Easy (+6.1), ME (+7.3), and Moderate (+18.3).

section_difficulty_estimate.description: Per-section difficulty estimated by applying each pack's difficulty proportions to the section's item count within that pack. Rotation-group templating distributes difficulty labels evenly across sections within a pack, making the proportional estimate reliable.

A.assessment: Section A requires calculation proficiency (financial ratios, cash flow indirect method, revenue recognition journal entries). Estimated only 13 Difficult items (3.4%) vs 94 needed (25%). Pack A contributes 0 Difficult; all 13 come from Packs B/C/D/E. Pack A Section A has zero items above Moderate.

B.assessment: Largest section (500 items). Most calculation-intensive domain (master budget, cash budget, variance forecasting, learning curves). Should have the HIGHEST Difficult and VD counts. Estimated 17 Difficult (3.4%) — 108 short of target. This is the single biggest difficulty gap in the repository. Pack B Section B has ~6 Difficult; Pack A has 0.

C.assessment: Mirrors Section B profile (same item count, same pack-level rotation). Performance management items (variance analysis, ROI/RI, balanced scorecard) require multi-step analysis. 17 Difficult items is inadequate.

D.assessment: Cost management domain (job costing, process costing, ABC, joint costs, CVP). Mixed calculation/conceptual. Profile mirrors Section A. DL-012 clone groups in Packs C/D Section D inflate the item count with rotation artifacts — difficulty labels within these groups are template-assigned, not calibrated.

E.assessment: Largest section (415 items). Predominantly conceptual (COSO, governance, fraud, ethics). Understand predominance is partially appropriate — but evaluation-level items (fraud risk assessment, control deficiency judgment) should be Difficult. Pack E Section E (115 items) is 77% Understand — the most extreme cognitive skew in the repository. DL-016 (metadata-block shift) additionally affects Section E items in Pack A.

F.assessment: Newest domain (technology, analytics, ERP, cybersecurity, AI/automation). Highest DL-031 risk — definitional items ('ERP stands for...') labeled Moderate(3). Estimated 79 Easy items may be an undercount if DL-031 is systematically inflating definitions to Moderate. DL-035 affects 39 Certified Domain F items with empty distractor EW slots. DL-036 found 40-item regex mismatch in Pack E R-series within this domain area.

applies_to_all_packs_and_sections: ZERO Very Difficult items (Difficulty 5) — 0 of 2540 items. CAQS target is 10% (254 items). This is a content-authoring gap, not a calibration error — no template module ever generated VD-level items.
Moderate (3) overweight in all sections — pool-wide 48.3% vs 30% target (+18.3pp). Every section is ~20-25pp over on Moderate.
Difficult (4) severe underweight in all sections — pool-wide 3.3% vs 25% target (-21.7pp). Every section is ~20pp under.
Understand cognitive over-reliance — 3 of 5 packs (A, C, E) are Understand-dominant. Pack E is 77% Understand.
Template-rotation difficulty assignment (not cognitive calibration) is the root cause — difficulty labels were assigned by position in 5-item groups, not by analyzing cognitive demand.

B_highest_priority.why: Largest section (500 items). Most calculation-intensive domain. Should have the most Difficult and VD items by topic nature — yet has only ~17 Difficult (3.4%). 108 Difficult items short of target.
specific_gaps: Master budget sequencing: multi-department budget preparation should be Difficult
Cash budget with borrowing constraints: multi-step calculation with conditional logic
Learning curve applications: P1B-B-119 had a wrong answer — systemic formula risk in this area
Flexible budget + variance reconciliation: integrated analysis shouldn't be Moderate
Sensitivity analysis / what-if: evaluation-level, should be Difficult or VD

E_F_dl031_vulnerability.why: Section E (conceptual: COSO, governance) and Section F (definitional: technology terms) are most vulnerable to DL-031 — definition-match items labeled Moderate(3) that should be Easy(1).
indicators: Section E: 415 items, conceptual domain, 48% Moderate — likely inflated
Section F: 374 items, newer domain, many definitional stems
Pack E: 77% Understand — definition-match pattern thrives in Understand items
Session 700 Layer 2: 6 of 7 sampled difficulty miscalibrations followed the definition-match pattern
DL-031 estimated scope: ~500 items pool-wide; Sections E and F likely over-represented
E_F_dl031_vulnerability.recommendation: Target Sections E and F for DL-031 recalibration first — highest ROI per item recalibrated.

A_D_calculation_gap.why: Sections A and D require calculation proficiency (financial statements, cost allocation) but have the same estimated Difficult count (13) as the conceptual sections. Calculation-heavy items at Moderate misrepresent their cognitive demand.
specific_gaps: Cash flow indirect method: multi-step with judgment calls — should be Difficult
Revenue recognition (ASC 606): 5-step model with performance obligations — should span Difficult
Job/process costing with WIP: multi-step with equivalent units — should be Difficult
Joint cost allocation (NRV, physical units): multi-method comparison — should be Difficult

cross_pack_inequality.why: A student answering Pack A gets zero Difficult items. A student answering Pack B gets 29 (5.8%). Same section topics, different difficulty exposure. This violates the CAQS principle of balanced assessment across equivalent forms.
cross_pack_inequality.impact: Learner experience varies significantly by pack — not by section. This is a delivery-pool composition risk, not just a calibration defect.

findings.finding: Pool-wide zero Very Difficult items. CAQS target is 10% (254 items). This is a content-authorship gap — no template module generated VD-level questions. The entire top tier of cognitive challenge is absent from the repository.
findings.remediation: Author ~254 new items at Difficulty 5, or recalibrate ~254 existing Difficult/Moderate items upward with enhanced distractor engineering.

findings.finding: Difficult items severely underweight. Pool-wide 85 items (3.3%) vs 25% target (635). Shortfall: 550 items. This affects all sections proportionally, but sections B and C have the largest absolute gaps (108 items short each).
findings.remediation: Recalibrate ~550 Moderate items upward where cognitive demand warrants it (multi-step calculations, evaluation/judgment items). Target Sections B and C first due to calculation intensity.

findings.finding: Blueprint item-count balance is excellent — all sections within 1.5pp of IMA CSO weight. Section E slight over (16.3% vs 15% target) is driven by Pack E's 40 R-series supplements. Pack D Section F has 74 items (1 short).

Pack A has ZERO Difficult items (unique deficit). 225 Pack A items are Certified — meaning the learner pool has no Difficult exposure from Pack A across any section. Combined with Pack A's 43.8% Moderate-Easy proportion, Pack A is the weakest pack for exam-realism.
findings.remediation: Recalibrate ~50-75 Pack A items from Moderate/M-Easy to Difficult. Target calculation-heavy items in Sections A, B, C, D first.

findings.finding: Section B has the largest absolute difficulty gap: ~17 Difficult vs 125 target (108 short). As the most calculation-intensive domain (budgeting, forecasting, learning curves), this misrepresents the domain's actual cognitive demand on the real CMA exam.
findings.impact: Candidates may be underprepared for the computational complexity of the actual CMA Part 1 Section B questions.

findings.finding: DL-031 (definition-match inflation) is likely concentrated in Sections E and F. Items where the stem defines a term and the correct answer is the term are systematically labeled Moderate(3). Section F especially — as the newest domain with many definitional items — may have 30-50% of its Moderate items mislabeled.
findings.verification: Requires per-item lexical overlap analysis (stem vs correct choice) on Sections E and F across all packs.

findings.finding: Pack B is the benchmark pack for difficulty calibration — it has the best spread (26% Easy, 19% ME, 49% Mod, 6% Diff), strongest Apply ratio (65%), and only Remember items (41). Use Pack B's distribution as the recalibration target for other packs.
findings.recommendation: Study Pack B's item characteristics to understand what template configuration produced its superior calibration.

findings.finding: Cross-pack difficulty inequality creates uneven learner experience. A student taking a Pack A-heavy session sees 0 Difficult items; a Pack B-heavy session sees 29. This violates equivalent-forms fairness. The delivery engine should randomize across packs to mitigate, but the underlying calibration defect should be fixed.
findings.recommendation: Implement delivery-pool difficulty stratification to ensure each session draws Difficult items proportionally across packs.

findings.finding: Pack E cognitive skew (77% Understand) is appropriate for Sections E and F content but not for Sections A-D. Pack E's Section A-D items share the same 77% Understand profile as Sections E-F — suggesting the cognitive label was assigned by pack template, not by per-item cognitive assessment.
findings.remediation: Verify that Pack E Sections A-D Apply items haven't been mislabeled as Understand.

findings.finding: Pack D Section F has 74 Section-field matches vs 75 expected. The 75th item exists (500 QuestionIDs confirmed, difficulty counts sum to 500) but its Section field doesn't match the standard regex pattern — likely a line-split or formatting artifact. Investigation deferred.
findings.action: Identify the 75th Section F item in Pack D via boundary-aware object parsing.

execution_constraints: Per-item recalibration requires reading stem + choices + CorrectChoice — automated lexical overlap scan can identify DL-031 candidates but cannot replace cognitive judgment
